economy.summary: In her campaign announcement she said families across the district are working hard but many still feel economic pressure and uncertainty, that government has a responsibility to create stability and opportunity, and listed affordability among her campaign's core issues.
economy.short: Cites affordability and economic pressure; wants stability and opportunity.

taxes.summary: Cites property tax pressures as a consequence of state funding systems, drawing on her experience as Crestwood School Board president; her announcement does not detail a specific tax proposal.
taxes.short: Cites property tax pressures tied to state funding systems.

education.summary: Says her campaign will support strong public schools; as president of the Crestwood School Board she cites how state funding systems affect education, special education, and local communities.
education.short: Supports strong public schools; cites state funding system effects.

healthcare.summary: Lists access to healthcare among the core economic and quality-of-life issues her campaign will focus on; her announcement does not detail specific proposals.
healthcare.short: Lists healthcare access as core campaign focus; no detailed proposals.

energy.summary: Lists rising energy costs among the core issues facing families in the district; her announcement frames this as a cost-of-living concern and does not detail energy or environmental policy positions.
energy.short: Cites rising energy costs as core issue; no policy detail.

economy.summary: Opposed HB 500's proposed elimination of the Local Resource Manufacturing Tax Credit tied to a planned natural gas plant in Newport Township, saying investment goes where it is welcomed and that the credit created a pathway to put thousands of Northeast Pennsylvania workers on the job.
economy.short: Supports manufacturing tax credit to attract investment and jobs.

taxes.summary: Voted for the $50.8 billion 2026-27 state budget, calling preservation of the Rainy Day Fund a fiscal victory and noting it limited spending growth and avoided new business taxes; he criticized its reliance on a 'Medicaid roll' that he said shifts costs into the future.
taxes.short: Voted for 2026-27 budget; praised reserves, no new business taxes.

abortion.summary: Describes himself as personally pro-life and says he has never supported an outright ban on abortion; supports exceptions for rape, incest, and the life of the mother, and has said he favors limiting abortion after 16 to 20 weeks rather than Pennsylvania's current 24-week limit.
abortion.short: Personally pro-life; opposes outright ban; favors earlier week limit.

education.summary: Supports school choice, saying state funding should follow individual students to increase access to private schools; he has said he is not advocating defunding public schools but thinks there needs to be more competition.
education.short: Supports school choice with funding following students; more competition.

energy.summary: Opposes the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and bans on natural gas, and supports government cooperation and tax incentives for reclaiming former mining sites.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI and natural gas bans; supports mine reclamation incentives.

guns.summary: Supports constitutional carry and has said red flag laws raise due process concerns; he opposes defunding police, advocated hiring more officers while on Plymouth Borough Council, and supported the 2022 Officer John Wilding Law making it a felony to harm officers while fleeing arrest.
guns.short: Supports constitutional carry; questions red-flag laws; backs police.
